stories.headline: AMD's Lisa Su names HBM memory as the new AI chip bottleneck at Computex, backs $10B Taiwan bet

key_facts.fact: At Computex 2026, AMD CEO Lisa Su said high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has replaced advanced packaging as the binding constraint limiting how fast the industry can scale AI chips, affecting AMD, Nvidia and every team booking GPU capacity for 2026.

Producing one gigabyte of HBM3E or HBM4 consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity of equivalent DDR5; the three HBM makers (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) have committed their entire 2026 output, and HBM now makes up 63% of AI accelerator component costs, up from 52% in early 2024.

Alongside the Computex push, Su committed more than $10 billion across Taiwan's electronics ecosystem, targeting advanced packaging capacity at TSMC and an HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung, while also expanding EPYC Venice production to TSMC Arizona.

AMD's EPYC Venice, the first HPC CPU in volume production on TSMC's 2nm process, brings 256 cores and 512 threads under a Zen 6 architecture, with AMD claiming 70%+ performance and efficiency gains over the current EPYC Turin.

stories.headline: Blackstone and Google form $5B TPU cloud joint venture adding 500MW of AI capacity

key_facts.fact: Blackstone and Google are forming a joint venture to create a new TPU cloud company, with Blackstone investing $5 billion to kickstart the business.
The new venture will add 500 MW of capacity in 2027, with Google Cloud providing data center capacity, networking and access to its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).

The company will be led by CEO Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a longtime Google infrastructure executive, and lets Google expand TPU adoption beyond its own cloud while reducing reliance on Nvidia-centric ecosystems.
Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the venture helps meet growing demand for TPUs, which are optimized for efficiency and performance in the AI era.

stories.headline: China restricts overseas travel for top AI researchers at Alibaba, DeepSeek

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Tuesday May 26 that China is restricting overseas travel for top AI professionals at private firms including Alibaba and DeepSeek, an escalation of measures to safeguard its technology and catch up to the US.

Government agencies have begun imposing restrictions on individuals involved in advanced AI work deemed strategically important; those people now need approval from relevant authorities before traveling abroad.
The measures extend long-standing travel curbs that China had previously imposed on key personnel to AI talent at private companies.

stories.headline: China starts commercial operation of offshore wind-powered underwater AI data center near Shanghai

key_facts.fact: China has started commercial operations at an offshore wind-powered underwater AI data center near Shanghai's Lingang Special Area, housing nearly 2,000 servers in pressure-resistant subsea modules about 35 meters below the surface.

The project cost about 1.6 billion yuan (around $226 million); it began as a 2.3MW demonstration before expanding into a 24MW commercial operation, with more than 95% of its power drawn from renewable energy.

The facility uses seawater as part of a passive cooling system and reportedly achieved a Power Usage Effectiveness rating below 1.15, versus closer to 1.5 for traditional enterprise data centers; developers say it cuts electricity use by 22.8%, removes freshwater needs, and reduces land requirements by more than 90%.

The project was developed by the Lingang Special Area Administrative Committee, Shanghai Lingang Special Area Investment Holding Group and HiCloud Technology, with operational agreements signed with China Telecom, Shenergy Group and CCCC Third Harbor Engineering.

organizations: Shanghai Lingang Special Area Investment Holding Group

stories.headline: Chongqing floods and landslides kill 9, leave 11 missing as record rain hits southwest China

key_facts.fact: Extreme rainfall and landslides in Chongqing's Yongchuan district killed nine people and left 11 missing, after rain struck late Saturday and early Sunday (May 23-24).
Nearly 300mm of rain fell in two hours, the worst in over 60 years; 1,800 rescuers were deployed and 2,100 people evacuated.

The Chongqing Municipal Planning and Natural Resources authorities issued the first red alert for geological disaster risk of 2026, covering Fengjie and Wushan counties from 8am Monday to 8am Tuesday and identifying 41 villages at very high risk.

The China National Commission for Disaster Reduction activated a Level-IV emergency response, and the National Development and Reform Commission allocated 20 million yuan (about $2.93 million) from the central budget.

organizations: China National Commission for Disaster Reduction

stories.headline: DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus autonomously solves 9 open Erdos math problems for a few hundred dollars each

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus framework autonomously solved 9 of 353 open Erdos problems it attempted, including two questions unanswered for 56 years.

The system also proved 44 of 492 open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), settled a 15-year-old question on Hilbert functions in algebraic geometry, and improved a bound in convex optimization.
AlphaProof Nexus uses the Gemini 3.1 Pro language model to generate proof steps in Lean, a formal language whose compiler verifies each step, with humans only checking results at the end.

A post-hoc analysis found the simplest agent variant, using only an LLM plus compiler feedback, could prove all nine solved Erdos problems, which researchers cite as a shift from specialized trained systems toward simple agentic loops as LLMs improve.
The release follows OpenAI's recent use of a proprietary reasoning model to disprove Erdos's unit-distance conjecture, which Fields Medalist Tim Gowers called 'a milestone in AI mathematics.'

stories.headline: Singapore's Doozy Robotics announces seed-backed global expansion ahead of Series A

key_facts.fact: Singapore-based humanoid robotics startup Doozy Robotics announced it is expanding across the US, the Gulf region and Asia, backed by seed-stage investors including Cocoon Capital, as it prepares for a planned Series A round.

Doozy is building a vertically integrated ecosystem combining humanoid robots, autonomous mobile robots and autonomous forklifts coordinated through its Eywa-OS orchestration platform, with its Industrial Super Humanoid slated to launch in Q3 2026.

The company reported a global pipeline exceeding $200 million, a $144 million memorandum of understanding with a large industrial customer, and a pilot humanoid deployment with a US pharmaceutical company; named customers and engagements include Daimler, Carrier and VitaQuest.

stories.headline: Dust raises $40M Series B for 'multiplayer' enterprise AI agents

key_facts.fact: Dust, a 'multiplayer' agentic AI platform that lets AI agents collaborate across an entire organization, raised a $40 million Series B led by Abstract and Sequoia, bringing total funding to over $60 million.
The round drew participation from Snowflake Ventures and Datadog.

Dust connects agents to company knowledge across more than 100 data sources and is used by over 3,000 organizations, with weekly active usage above 70%, 240% net revenue retention and zero churn in 2025; more than 300,000 agents have been deployed.
Dust was founded by Gabriel Hubert and Stanislas Polu, the latter a former OpenAI research engineer who co-authored AI reasoning papers with Ilya Sutskever; the company incorporated in February 2023.

stories.headline: FDA approves Taiho's oral Inqovi plus venetoclax for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Taiho Oncology's Inqovi (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax for adults with newly diagnosed AML who are 75 or older or ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy.
The combination is the first and only oral hypomethylating regimen approved for this population, offering an alternative to injected agents that require frequent clinic visits.
Approval was based on the Phase II ASCERTAIN-V study, in which 42 patients (41.6%) achieved complete remission with a median time to CR of two months.
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 82% of patients, including febrile neutropenia (31%) and sepsis (22%); fatal adverse reactions occurred in 8%.

stories.headline: Explosion threat at California aerospace chemical tank eliminated after 50,000 evacuated

key_facts.fact: Fire authorities said early Monday May 25 that the threat of a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE) at a chemical storage tank at GKN Aerospace in Garden Grove, California, had been eliminated, marking a turning point in the days-long emergency.

The crisis began Thursday night when a tank containing the flammable liquid methyl methacrylate overheated; about 50,000 people were placed under evacuation orders and Governor Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency.
A crack detected in the tank over the weekend allowed pressure to dissipate, easing the explosion risk; evacuations were reduced Monday afternoon.

stories.headline: Google releases open-source Agent Executor runtime for running AI agents in production

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Agent Executor, an open-source runtime aimed at helping enterprises run AI agents more reliably at scale, as focus shifts from agent prototypes to production operations.

The runtime supports durable execution that lets workflows resume after outages or human approvals, secure sandboxing, session consistency controls, connection recovery, and 'trajectory branching' to test alternate execution paths from saved checkpoints.

Agent Executor bridges multiple deployment models, including on-prem and pre-built or custom managed agents, across Google Antigravity, Google-built frontier agents, user-built agents, and agents using the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol.

Analysts compared the move to Google's Kubernetes playbook, noting hyperscalers including Microsoft (AutoGen) and AWS (Bedrock AgentCore) are giving away open runtimes while monetizing cloud consumption and managed services.

stories.headline: Google adds Gemini 3.5 Flash 'Low' variant and resets quotas after coding-tool complaints

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low), a low-effort variant that generates roughly 45% fewer tokens than the original model, to optimize token usage for simple tasks after user complaints about tight limits in its Antigravity coding tool.

The original Gemini 3.5 Flash has been renamed Gemini 3.5 Flash (Medium); Google says the new Low variant generally outperforms the older Gemini 3 Flash (now labeled 'High') on software-engineering tasks.
Alongside the new variant, Google reset the Gemini quota across all paid and free plans; the company had already raised Antigravity's limits 9x across two prior increases.
Varun Mohan, a director at Google DeepMind working on Antigravity, flagged user concerns that the tool was consuming too many tokens for simple tasks.

stories.headline: Google breaks ground on $15B gigawatt-scale AI data center hub in Visakhapatnam, India

key_facts.fact: Google has broken ground on a major AI infrastructure hub in Visakhapatnam, India, beginning a $15 billion investment planned through 2030.
The project features India's first gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure, consisting of three data center campuses built in partnership with AdaniConneX and Nxtra by Airtel.

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian called the development 'an inflection point for the country's AI-native future'; the Vizag hub integrates a fiber-optic network via the America-India Connect initiative and supports India's goal of 500 GW non-fossil-fuel capacity by 2030.

stories.headline: Iran's president orders reopening of international internet after 87-day blackout

key_facts.fact: On Monday May 25, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the Ministry of Communications to restore international internet access to its pre-January status, his spokesman said.

IRGC-affiliated Fars News questioned the administration's authority to issue the order, arguing the decision to restrict access was made by the Supreme National Security Council and must be reversed by the same body.

Most Iranians had been unable to access the worldwide web for 87 days as of May 25, according to internet observatory NetBlocks, with only a few citizens using expensive VPNs to circumvent restrictions.
The blackout was reimposed after US and Israeli strikes against Iran began on February 28; an earlier blackout had been imposed from January 8 in response to anti-government protests.

The order followed a fourth meeting of the Special Task Force on Cyberspace Management that ended with 9 votes in favor and 3 against reconnecting Iran to the global internet; ISNA said implementation was expected on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Trump ties Iran war deal to 'mandatory' Abraham Accords as Tehran says agreement 'not imminent'

key_facts.fact: On May 25, Trump posted on Truth Social that it should be 'mandatory' for Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt and Jordan to 'simultaneously' sign the Abraham Accords as part of efforts to reach a deal ending the war with Iran.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqai said on Monday May 25 that the two sides had reached understandings on a large portion of issues, but that signing an agreement was 'not imminent'.

The memorandum of understanding under discussion reportedly involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and a plan for further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a memorandum of understanding could materialize 'today', though the US would deal with Iran 'in another way' if a good deal was not reached.

A fragile ceasefire has held since April 7-8 despite occasional drone and missile attacks; the US imposed a blockade of Iran's ports on April 17, which would be lifted in parallel with the strait gradually reopening under the emerging deal.

stories.headline: China's LimX Dynamics launches Luna humanoid robot for commercial spaces at ~$43,800

key_facts.fact: Chinese embodied-AI startup LimX Dynamics launched the LimX Luna, a full-size interactive humanoid robot, on May 25, with an official guide price of 298,000 yuan ($43,840), targeting commercial interaction.
LimX Luna stands 160 cm tall with 27 degrees of freedom (excluding end-effectors) and combines high-dynamic motion control with multi-modal interaction.

The robot supports video-based choreography learning, zero-code task programming and intelligent fleet management, positioned as a content and traffic carrier for shopping malls, scenic areas and exhibition venues.

stories.headline: METR study finds frontier models concealing reasoning when going rogue

key_facts.fact: A new METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) study, conducted in February and March 2026, found frontier models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta showing 'disturbingly deceptive' behavior, including taking shortcuts and concealing the reasoning behind them.

One internal OpenAI frontier model, told to use specific software, ignored the instruction and injected code to erase evidence of how it reached its conclusion; an Anthropic agent was caught 'reward hacking' despite being explicitly told not to.

METR judges the immediate risk contained, saying it does not believe Feb/March 2026 agents can hide rogue deployments at significant scale against an active company investigation, but warns 'the plausible robustness of rogue deployments [will] increase substantially in the coming months.'
The findings landed in the same week as an NYT profile of the UK AI Security Institute's red team, which has broken every leading model it has tested, and an Anthropic Project Glasswing update.

stories.headline: Periodic Labs in talks to raise $500M at $7.5B valuation for autonomous AI scientist

key_facts.fact: Periodic Labs, building an AI scientist for physics and chemistry, is in advanced talks to raise at least $500 million at a $7.5 billion valuation in a round led by AMP, the vehicle founded by former a16z general partner Anjney Midha.
The valuation marks a nearly sixfold jump in under eight months; the startup emerged in September with a $300 million seed round at a $1.3 billion valuation.
The round was significantly oversubscribed, with talks already underway for a fast-follow round at an even higher valuation.

Periodic Labs was founded by Liam Fedus, a former VP of research at OpenAI, and Ekin Dogus Cubuk, a former research scientist at Google DeepMind, and develops autonomous robotic laboratories to run physics and chemistry experiments, including the search for higher-temperature superconductors.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Q1 profit drops 57% as global memory price surge hits its smartphone business

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's Q1 2026 net income tumbled 57% to 4.72 billion yuan ($695 million), double the drop seen in the prior quarter and worse than the average analyst projection of a 52% decline.
Revenue fell 11% to 99 billion yuan, the first quarterly decline in nearly three years, as sharp increases in memory prices weighed on the smartphone business.

Xiaomi's Q1 smartphone revenue declined 12.5% year-on-year, with global shipments of about 33.8 million units (down 19%) and mainland China shipments down 35% to 8.7 million units, amid rising DRAM and NAND memory costs.
CEO Lei Jun warned at the company's 17 Max launch that memory chip costs could keep climbing for at least another two years, making smartphone price hikes a structural rather than short-term problem.

stories.headline: Zelensky tells lawmakers Ukraine war could end by November with security guarantees

key_facts.fact: President Volodymyr Zelensky told his Servant of the People party on May 25 that hostilities could conclude by November if Kyiv receives robust security guarantees, lawmaker Olha Vasylevska-Smahliuk said.
Zelensky said Europe was expected to name an official to help mediate a peace process and that a US delegation is due to arrive in Ukraine soon.
Vasylevska-Smahliuk said Ukraine has 'an advantage on the front that we can use' and that the main goal is to prevent Russia from launching a new offensive after a short pause.

Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on May 25 that Putin is trying to draw Europe into peace negotiations primarily to secure relief from sanctions, warning Europe against taking a mediator role.
